title: Shadow Routing Visualizer — private cluster routing & cost projection prototype
creator: Aisha Kumar
description: Design and prototype an interactive "shadow routing visualizer" for the Private/VPC console. The visualizer helps platform operators simulate traffic routing across private clusters, compare latency/cost tradeoffs for different routing policies (regional primary, cross-region failover, model-variant fallback), and preview rollout impact before applying changes. The UI should integrate with the Console's rollout controls and cost panel so operators can see projected token cost deltas and request paths for a sample workload.
user_stories: As a tenant operator I want to simulate routing policies for a specific service so I can choose the lowest-latency path while keeping within budget
As a platform engineer I want to preview how a canary rollout will route traffic across dedicated pools and fall back to hosted models so I can verify safety before applying changes
As a product manager I want quick cost delta projections for routing decisions so I can approve changes with finance constraints in mind
acceptance_criteria: Interactive topology canvas shows clusters, regions, and available model variants with clear latency and cost overlays
Operator can toggle policies (latency-first, cost-first, region-affinity) and see per-route projected P50/P95 latency and monthly token cost delta for a supplied traffic profile
Preview mode links to existing rollout controls and can generate a deterministic 'shadow traffic' plan that engineers can export as a JSON for testing
Prototype demonstrates failure-mode visualization: when a cluster is degraded, the UI highlights fallback routes and the change in cost/latency
Design includes accessible color palette, keyboard interactions for canvas controls, and a compact table export for finance reviews
engineering_feedback: 2026-02-12 - Priya: prefer server-side simulation API rather than running heavy sim in the browser; expose a /simulate-routing endpoint
2026-02-20 - Backend: require a sampling mode for traffic profiles to avoid leaking tenant data; suggested sample weights parameter
2026-03-03 - Runtime team: KV cache and batching behavior makes P95 sensitive to sequence length; recommend adding sequence-length distribution input to simulation
design_decisions: Use a two-pane layout: left canvas for topology and route overlays, right panel for policy controls, cost projections, and timeline scrubber
Represent cost as a stacked bar (model compute + egress) with hover breakdowns; latency uses interpolated heat contours on edges
Default policy presets: latency-first, cost-first, region-affinity; advanced mode exposes per-route weight sliders
Export format will use the existing rollout JSON shape to simplify handoff to the rollout service
tradeoffs: Client-side simulation gives instant feedback but can be inaccurate without runtime telemetry; decided to fetch baseline telemetry from server and run lightweight diffs in the browser
Showing both cost and latency at once increases visual complexity; we prioritize latency heatmap + concise cost bar to reduce cognitive load
Precise token-cost modeling requires payload-level info which we cannot send for privacy; we will accept user-provided sample profiles for accurate cost projections
accessibility_notes: Ensure color contrast for heatmap overlays meets WCAG AA on all palettes
Keyboard-first interactions: nodes focusable, arrow keys for panning canvas, space to open route details
Provide CSV export for finance teams who rely on spreadsheets
